Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Then God said to Moses: 'Go in to Pharaoh — for I have strengthened his heart and the hearts of his officers, so that I may bring these my plagues upon them.
translations.2: And so that you may recount to your son and to your son's son what I have struck the Egyptians with by force, and my plagues which I have brought upon them — that you may know that I am God.'
translations.3: And Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and said to him: 'Thus says God, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to submit before Me? Release my people, that they may serve Me.
translations.4: For if you refuse to release my people — behold, I am bringing at daybreak the locusts within your territory,
translations.5: and they shall cover the eye of the land, so that no one shall be able to look upon it; and they shall eat the remainder of the remnant that was left to you from the hail, and they shall eat every tree growing for you from the wilderness.'
translations.6: And your houses shall be filled with them, and the houses of your officers and the houses of the rest of the Egyptians — the like of which your fathers and your fathers' fathers have not seen, since their being upon the earth until this day.' Then he turned and went out from before Pharaoh.
translations.7: And the officers of Pharaoh said to him: 'How long shall this be a snare about our necks? Release the people, that they may serve God their Lord — before you see Egypt utterly destroyed.'
translations.8: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them: 'Go, serve God your Lord. But who and who are those who are going?'
translations.9: Moses said: 'With our young and with our elders we shall go; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flock and with our cattle we shall go — for the festival of God belongs to us.'
translations.10: He said to them: 'So be it — may God be with you — just as I would release you and your children! Behold, I see evil facing you.'
translations.11: It is not thus. Let the men among you go and serve God — for that is indeed what you are seeking.' And he drove them out from before Pharaoh.
translations.12: And God said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt on account of the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt and eat all its herbage — all that the hail left.'
translations.13: And Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and God drove the qibla-wind through the land all that day and its night; and when morning came, the qibla-wind carried the locusts.
translations.14: And the locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled throughout all its territory — very greatly; before it there had been no such locusts as these, and after it there shall not be so.
translations.15: And it covered the eye of all the land until it was darkened; and it ate all the herbage of the land, and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left; and there remained nothing of the green in the trees or in the herbage of the wilderness throughout all the land of Egypt.
translations.16: Then Pharaoh hastened and called for Moses and Aaron, and said: 'I have sinned against God your Lord, and against you.
translations.17: And now — bear my sin this time, and intercede with God your Lord, that He remove from me this sheer death.'
translations.18: And when he went out from before him, he interceded with God.
translations.19: And God turned a very fierce west wind, and it carried the locusts, and the Sea of Qulzum (Red Sea) received them; not a single locust remained in all the land of Egypt.
translations.20: And God hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not release the sons of Israel.
translations.21: And God said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand toward the sky — there shall be darkness over all the land of Egypt, after the fading of the darkness of night.'
translations.22: And Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and there was a thick darkness throughout all the land of Egypt — three days.
translations.23: No person saw his fellow, and no person rose from his place for three days; but for all the sons of Israel there was light in their dwellings.
translations.24: And Pharaoh called for Moses, and said: 'Go, serve God — only your flock and your cattle leave behind; your children may go with you.'
translations.25: Moses said to him: 'Nay, you yourself shall give us sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may offer them to God our Lord.
translations.26: And our livestock shall go with us too — not a hoof shall remain from them; for from them we shall take to serve God our Lord; and we do not know how great a measure of what we shall serve God with, until we arrive there.'
translations.27: And God hardened his heart, and he did not will to release them.
translations.28: Pharaoh said to him: 'Go from me — beware lest you see my face again; for on the day you see my face, you shall be put to death.'
translations.29: Moses said to him: 'You have spoken rightly. I shall not see your face again.'
